title: Always On Display Widget - Testers wanted
symptom: Users testing the new xDrip Always On Display widget report that the widget sometimes jumps, overlaps the clock or fingerprint icon, and lags briefly when unlocking; in some cases the clock or glucose values are unreadable because they overlap.
cause: The widget intentionally moves around to reduce screen burn-in, but the positions of the clock/fingerprint icons on the Always On Display vary between Android versions and phone models, causing the widget to overlap them.
fix: Der-Schubi contributed pull request #3153 to let users choose where on screen the AOD widget moves, and as of the February 07, 2024 release users can control where the widget moves. Documentation is available at https://navid200.github.io/xDrip/docs/Display/AOD.html.
evidence_quote: Thanks to @Der-Schubi, you can now (as of the February 07, 2024 release) control where on screen the widget moves.
